en: Salutations to the glorious Supreme Self.
Now, the hymn of praise to the venerable Śrī Svāmī Śukadeva, the crest-jewel of the Paramahaṃsas and an Avadhūta:
I bow to the Avadhūta, who is free from latent impressions, devoid of desire, liberated from all defects, without support, and free from fear. (1)

I bow to the Avadhūta, who is free from possessiveness and egoism, for whom a clod of earth, a stone, and gold are equal, and who remains steadfast with equanimity toward both suffering and happiness.
Having truly realized the self as one, imperishable, and free from passion, fear, and anger—I bow to that Avadhūta. 3.
I am not the body, nor is the body mine; I am not the vital breath, for I am indeed consciousness.
Having realized this, I bow to the Avadhūta who is truly contented.
"Everything is merely conceptual construction; the Self is eternally liberated.
Having realized this, I bow to the Avadhūta who is truly contented. 5.
I bow to that Avadhūta, whose karmas have been burnt by the fire of knowledge, who is free from desire and volition, and who is devoid of both the rejectable and the acceptable.
I bow to the Avadhūta, who, through the mere cessation of delusion and by the simple recovery of his true nature, is free from sorrow and effortless.
Having ascertained that the Self is Brahman, and having transcended the imagined notions of existence and non-existence,
I bow to the Avadhūta who sits happily in equanimity.
I bow to that Avadhūta who, by his very nature, does not desire pleasure or enjoyment, and who is content with whatever comes to him by chance. 9.
I bow to that great-souled Avadhūta, whose mind is never altered by either censure or praise, and who finds delight only in the Self. 10.
I bow to the Avadhūta, who remains perpetually in the waking state as if in a dream, free from anxiety, and whose self consists of pure consciousness. 11.
I bow to that Avadhūta who has neither the hateful nor the beloved, for whom there is nothing auspicious or inauspicious, and who is devoid of the knowledge of duality. 12.
I bow to that Avadhūta who does not perceive the world as inert matter, but perceives it as consisting of consciousness, eternally united, transcending the qualities (guṇas). 13.
I bow to the Avadhūta, who purifies the three worlds by his mere sight; he is the moving holy ford (tīrtha), the purifier himself. 14.
I bow to the partless, actionless, tranquil, stainless, supreme nectar, the infinite support of the universe, the Avadhūta. 15.
Thus ends the Avadhūtāṣṭaka.
